summary: PR #71 bumps the single transitive dev dependency nanoid from 3.3.17 to 3.3.18 in apps/web/package-lock.json to clear GHSA-2v37-7h3g-55p8. Every material claim was re-derived independently. The central open question -- whether the committed sha1 integrity digest pins the true public bytes, given that this machine's npm registry is an internal mirror and the public registry is unreachable here -- is now CLOSED by direct measurement on a GitHub-hosted runner resolving from the real public registry. dist.shasum for nanoid@3.3.18 equals f66a2de1199ffde0fcf21c8a5f13106b1c081913, the 5713-byte public tarball hashes to that same value, its base64 form 9mot4Rmf/eD88hyKXxMQaxwIGRM= is byte-identical to the committed integrity, and npm ci from the committed lockfile succeeded with integrity enforcement (exit 0). The green gate is caused by the vulnerability being fixed, not by any weakening of the check.

digest_provenance_L1.why_it_was_open: The build machine's npm registry is an internal mirror, verified by SHA-256 of the hostname without ever recording the value: local host hash 2283DBF20C50 versus public registry.npmjs.org hash 0DC11026AC75, not equal. Direct HTTPS to the public registry from this machine fails at TLS and the agent web-fetch path failed at transport level. All builder-side derivations therefore traced through one mirror, which is one measurement repeated rather than independent agreement.
digest_provenance_L1.independent_source_used: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest runner. Evaluator-owned temporary probe workflow on a throwaway branch created from the base commit, checking out the PR head read-only. The PR branch was never touched. Branch deleted after use; run logs retained as durable evidence.

controls.why_the_positive_control_is_non_vacuous: The 3.3.17 digest was committed to this repository BEFORE this work began, so the method recovers a pre-existing datum that the builder did not author, from a source that never touched this machine. That is qualitatively stronger than self-consistency. The 3.3.16 digest differs from the subject, so the method also discriminates between versions and would have failed had the derivation been wrong.

digest_provenance_L1.why_npm_ci_is_the_strong_form: npm ci verifies each package's declared integrity against the bytes actually downloaded and aborts with EINTEGRITY on mismatch. Succeeding against the real public registry using the committed lockfile is a byte-level proof of the digest. This is categorically different from npm audit, which performs no install, downloads no tarball and verifies no hash.

The 'Node format and lint' job runs npm ci at the repository ROOT with no working-directory, then Prettier and ESLint. apps/web receives only 'npm audit --audit-level=high' in the Dependency audit job, and npm audit performs no install. Corroborated from a second independent direction: the root package.json declares no workspaces, so a root npm ci cannot reach apps/web. Consequence: apps/web's 9 test files / 110 tests, tsc -b type-checking and the production build never run in CI. Not a defect of this PR and explicitly not grounds for failing it.

postcss_resolution.status: CONFIRMED correct; postcss needs no change
postcss_resolution.detail: The pinned and installed postcss is 8.5.25 and its lockfile entry declares nanoid ^3.3.16. 3.3.18 satisfies ^3.3.16 and equally satisfies the ^3.3.17 required by registry-latest 8.5.26, so both readings reproduce and both are satisfied. postcss is the ONLY package in the tree declaring a nanoid dependency, so no second consumer imposes a conflicting range.

findings_not_disclosed_by_the_builder.finding: The lockfile's integrity digests are sha1 across the board: 335 sha1- and 1 sha512-, identical on base and head. The new entry correctly matches that convention. But the public registry's own canonical integrity for nanoid@3.3.18 is sha512-DTg4MJbGMWkfi6VZFdNt2/caMbQy4Ou+Op/hJQvGEWcnVfoA1QA+xzRKAzw9jD6+GVOOeYr/mIcuDSdug6F6+w==, whereas the repository pins the weaker sha1 form derived from dist.shasum. npm enforces whichever algorithm the lockfile declares, so the install is still verified and my public npm ci confirms these exact bytes. Pre-existing and repository-wide, NOT introduced by this PR, but sha1 is a weaker supply-chain primitive than sha512 and the lockfile-wide sha1 pattern is itself a fingerprint of mirror-mediated lockfile generation. Worth a separate slice.

nanoid is a DEV-ONLY dependency here (dev: true, reached solely through postcss, itself dev). The advisory's exposure is build-time rather than in shipped product code, which lowers real-world severity relative to the raw 'high' label. This does not reduce the value of fixing it and does not change the disposition.
